validity.recommendation: P2615 and P2614 ("Puerto Libertad Expansion") describe the SAME physical FERC-authorized project -- the Sierrita Gas Pipeline Expansion Project (Docket Nos. CP18-37-000/CP18-38-000: one new 15,900 hp compressor station in Pima County, Arizona, on existing Line No. 2177, filed Dec 21, 2017, certificated ~Oct 2018, placed in service April 12, 2020). Retire/merge P2614 into P2615 rather than carry both as separate capacity increments -- P2614's own deep-sweep shard (rows/P2614.json) independently reached the same conclusion from the P2614 side and already recommends the merge. P2615's own recorded figures (320 MMcf/d, $56M, 2020 start) are the ones that check out cleanly against primary sources; keep this row as the surviving record.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION for P2615 itself are solid and well-sourced (see fills[] below): Kinder Morgan's own SEC 8-Ks (Q4-2019, filed 2020-01-22, and Q1-2020, filed 2020-04-22) both describe 'the approximately $56 million Sierrita Gas Pipeline Expansion Project ... increase the pipeline's capacity by approximately 323,000 Dth/d to 524,000 Dth/d, and consists of a new 15,900 horsepower compressor station in Pima County, Arizona,' with the Q1-2020 filing adding 'was placed in service on April 12, 2020.' EIA's Today in Energy (independent, government) names 'the 0.32 Bcf/d Sierrita Pima Expansion' verbatim -- an exact match to this row's segment name and its recorded Capacity=320.00 MMcf/d -- and states it 'was also completed in early 2020.' The Federal Register (via govinfo.gov, independent of gem.wiki) confirms Sierrita filed its application Dec 21, 2017 and that FERC opened environmental review of the 'Sierrita Compressor Expansion Project' in Pima County in 2018. All of this cleanly matches P2615's existing Capacity/SegmentCost/Start/Location values -- no evidence problem on THIS row's own numbers. The problem is that P2614 (sheet_row for 'Puerto Libertad Expansion', Capacity recorded as 427 MMcf/d) appears to be a duplicate entry for the exact same compressor-station project rather than a second, additive expansion phase: no primary source I found (KMI's own 10-Ks/8-Ks, EIA, Federal Register, Utility Dive per P2614's shard) describes two separate Sierrita expansion projects in this window, and KMI's FY2022 10-K reports Sierrita's TOTAL system capacity at only 0.52 Bcf/d (520 MMcf/d = 200 original + 320 Pima expansion), which leaves no room for an additional, non-overlapping 427 MMcf/d increment. 'Puerto Libertad' is most likely the name of the Sonora, Mexico destination town/market this SAME compressor expansion was built to serve (a separate, IEnova/CFE-owned Mexican pipeline, 'Sasabe-Puerto Libertad,' receives Sierrita's gas on the Mexican side), not a second US-side construction project. Net: this is a duplicate/consolidation issue across the row pair, not a defect in P2615's own sourced values.

cross_row_leads.facts: KMI's own Q1-2020 8-K exhibit describes exactly ONE Sierrita expansion project in this period: 'the approximately $56 million Sierrita Gas Pipeline Expansion Project ... was placed in service on April 12, 2020 ... increase the pipeline's capacity by approximately 323,000 Dth/d to 524,000 Dth/d, and consists of a new 15,900 horsepower compressor station in Pima County, Arizona.' This matches P2615's recorded Capacity (320 MMcf/d)/SegmentCost ($56M)/Start (2020) closely and gives NO indication of a second, separate 427 MMcf/d 'Puerto Libertad Expansion' project. Combined with EIA naming 'the 0.32 Bcf/d Sierrita Pima Expansion' verbatim and KMI's FY2022 10-K reporting Sierrita's TOTAL system capacity at only 0.52 Bcf/d (200 original + 320, no room for +427 more), P2614 (427 MMcf/d) is very likely a duplicate/erroneous record of this same P2615 project, not a genuine second expansion phase. P2614's own deep-sweep shard (rows/P2614.json, already produced) independently reached this same conclusion from the P2614 side and recommends retiring/merging it into P2615 -- route this confirmation there.
